title: The Lantern of the Lower Danube
premise: In 1848, on the marshy lower Danube, Ansel Yarrow — a pearl diver's daughter indentured to the Varga Trading Company — keeps the company's ledger of debts, names, and secrets. When imperial troops requisition the town and seize the ledger as evidence against her employer, Ansel realizes the book contains proof that would hang half the waterfront, including her own forged entries made to survive. She steals it back and must carry it past three army checkpoints to a neutral barge before the spring ice breaks and the river opens to warships. She delivers the ledger, but at the cost of betraying the one man who showed her kindness, and she leaves the Danube with a new name, no debt, and no home.
about_author: Rosalind Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing river-trade ledgers from the Habsburg frontier. Her fiction is known for its obsessive attention to paper, debt, and the quiet violence of bureaucracy.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet her diving for pearls at dawn and copying the Varga ledger by lamplight at night, measuring everything by weight and portability. She forges a small entry to erase a dead diver's debt — survival, not malice. Emotional beat: competence masking fear; the reader learns the ledger holds everyone's lives, including hers.

chapters.title: The Company's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Master Varga discovers the forgery but does not report her; instead he deepens her dependence, teaching her the ledger's coded margins where bribes and smuggled grain are recorded. A clerk, Tomas, quietly warns her that auditors are coming from Vienna. Emotional beat: gratitude tangled with entrapment — kindness as a leash.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Soldiers occupy the town, requisition warehouses, and confiscate the ledger as evidence against Varga. The divers are conscripted to salvage sunken army barges. Ansel watches the book — with her name in its margins — carried into the commandant's office. Emotional beat: vertigo; the instrument of her survival becomes the instrument of her destruction.

chapters.title: The Commandant's Offer
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Commandant Haller summons her to authenticate entries, testing whether she'll confirm Varga's crimes. He offers immunity if she testifies fully. She glimpses the ledger chained in his map room and memorizes the guard rotations. Emotional beat: temptation — freedom offered on a rope that can be pulled tight later.

chapters.title: Tomas's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Tomas. Tomas reveals he is an informant for the river smugglers and proposes stealing the ledger back together — he wants the margin codes destroyed, she wants her name cut out. They plan to copy pages rather than steal, splitting the risk. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With copied pages sewn into her diving coat, she passes the tollhouse checkpoint by hiding among corpses being shipped downstream for burial — trading on the soldiers' disgust. But a guard recognizes her father's old boat tag. Emotional beat: cold triumph curdling into exposure; she pays a bribe with her mother's pearl.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Frozen Ford
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the frozen ford, ice is breaking early; the crossing is closing. Haller has posted her description. Tomas arrives wounded — he was caught destroying the original margin codes and gave up her route under questioning. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief; the alliance breaks exactly when she needs it most.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with a flashback chapter in her father's voice. Trapped between checkpoints, she reads the copied pages by firelight and finds her father's death recorded as a deliberate drowning ordered by Varga — not an accident. Emotional beat: the past reweighed; rage gives her a reason beyond self-preservation to finish the run.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Climax. She crosses the cracking ford as the river opens, pursued by Haller's dragoons. Tomas appears one last time and turns the soldiers aside at the cost of his own capture. She reaches the neutral barge and hands over the ledger to the merchant-princes who will use it to topple Varga — and Haller. Emotional beat: victory that feels like spending herself.

chapters.title: A New Name on the Water
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. Varga hangs; Haller is recalled in disgrace; the town's debts are voided in the chaos. Ansel, now carrying nothing but a pearl and a blank page, signs onto a barge crew under a name she invents on the spot. Emotional beat: bittersweet freedom — identity finally chosen, at the price of everyone she knew.
